utility.notes: NorthWestern Energy is the well-established dominant electric utility for Billings, Montana's largest city.

value.name: NorthWestern Energy
value.notes: NorthWestern Energy is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: Billings, Montana's largest city, is the seat of Yellowstone County.

interconnection_url.notes: NorthWestern's own separate 'Home Solar Information' page explicitly states: 'NorthWestern Energy does not offer incentives for solar installations for residential customers,' and confirms net metering credits accumulate as a kWh balance that is available toward future bills only until the customer's selected annual settle-up month, at which point Montana law mandates the excess credit balance resets to zero (no rollover past that date, no cash-out).

battery_programs.notes: NorthWestern's own interconnection form restricts storage components on a net-metered system to storing/discharging only energy produced by that system (not energy drawn from NorthWestern's grid) — a technical eligibility rule, not a financial incentive program. No battery incentive program was found this session.

value.name: Detailed site plan (home/structure, electrical service meter, main service panel, interconnected sub-panels, all PV components, structure and panel square footage, IRC fire access pathways and ridge setbacks)
Mounting system evaluation by a Montana-licensed Professional Engineer (using minimum 30 psf non-reducible roof snow load, 110 mph ultimate wind speed, Exposure Category C)
One-line diagram (PV system type, module count/layout, circuit type, conductor/conduit sizing and types, equipment grounding conductor, fuse/breaker ratings)
Interconnected-components documentation with NEC Article 705 code references, plus photos of the meter main and interconnection point panels (overall view and manufacturer specification labels)
Site-specific equipment labeling diagram, including the NEC 705.10 directory ('typical'/generic labeling diagrams are not accepted)
Module specification sheets (UL 1703 listed) and inverter specification sheets ('utility interactive,' UL 1741, ground fault protection, rapid shutdown compliance)
NorthWestern Energy Level 1 Small Generator Facility Interconnection Request form, with equipment component list, one-line diagram, detailed site diagram, and product specification sheets
Exhibit A — Net Meter settle-up month selection (January, April, July, or October)
value.required_when: always, for installations requiring a net meter

required_documents.notes: The City's own Solar-Photovoltaic System Plan Requirements handout (Billings Building Division, dated 02/23) is unusually detailed and solar-specific.

inspection_steps.notes: Neither the City's own solar plan requirements handout nor NorthWestern Energy's own Level 1 interconnection form published a specific inspection sequence this session (the interconnection form implies a required 'in-service date' but does not itemize inspection steps) — left null rather than guessed.

value.notes: Per the City of Billings' own FAQ ('How long will it take to get a building permit?'), verbatim: 'Once a complete plan has been submitted, and special issues have been addressed... the initial review takes: Residential (single-family and duplex): 4-7 business days.' This is the general residential building-permit initial-review window, not a solar-specific figure. A previous research pass this session found this same figure only via third-party aggregator results and correctly left it unconfirmed; it has now been directly confirmed on the City's own FAQ page.

value.program_or_pathway: NorthWestern Energy's Level 1 Small Generator Facility Interconnection process — for systems with aggregate nameplate capacity (generation plus storage) of up to 50kW-AC using certified, publicly listed interconnection equipment.
other_conditions: Net-metered facilities may only be fueled by solar, wind, and/or hydropower, per NorthWestern's own interconnection form.
An external, visible, lockable AC disconnect switch must be located within 10 feet of the utility meter, unless NorthWestern Energy grants a case-by-case variance for a different location.

The customer must select an annual 'settle-up' month (January, April, July, or October); any unused excess energy credit balance resets to zero at that date, per Montana law — no ongoing rollover or cash-out.
NorthWestern Energy's own materials state it does not offer incentives for residential solar installations.
City of Billings mounting-system engineering calculations must use a minimum 30 psf non-reducible roof snow load, 110 mph ultimate wind speed, and Exposure Category C.

value.name: NorthWestern Energy Level 1 interconnection processing fee
value.unit: one-time, non-refundable, must accompany the Interconnection Request
value.notes: Per NorthWestern Energy's own Level 1 Small Generator Facility Interconnection Request form.

permit_fees.notes: No City of Billings building/electrical permit fee dollar figure was confirmed this session — the City's own site references an online fee calculator based on project valuation, but that calculator itself was not run this session.

rebates.notes: NorthWestern Energy's own 'Home Solar Information' page directly states it does not offer incentives for residential solar installations — a confirmed negative rather than an unresearched gap, but the field itself remains null per schema convention since there is no active program to describe.
